plan.goal: Cut in-tool and hook-path latency. Measured: storage is already free (append 17us, fold 1.64ms) — the cost is process spawns, O(sessions) projection write amplification, and model round trips.

tasks.title: Hot-path bundle split: dist/cli.js stub routes event|statusline to a small fast.js, everything else to full.js
Compile cache via the stub (module.enableCompileCache before the heavy import)
regenerateProjections rewrites plan.md + decisions.md + EVERY session .md on every append (27 files in token-optimization) — make it O(1) in touched sessions
Daemon + non-node hook shim: curl to a unix socket measured 6.9ms vs 64.5ms spawn; needs CLI fallback so correctness never depends on the daemon
Collapse the start-of-session round trip: SessionStart already injects the digest, so the agent's get_state/start_session call costs a model turn for data it has

payload.because: Measured: hooks were compiling 986KB (MCP SDK, chokidar, commander, cloud, doctor) to append one line. Hot path 56-64ms to 26-28ms; the slow path also improved 60ms to 47ms because the stub makes the compile cache actually apply. Falling through on unrecognized shapes keeps commander the single owner of the command surface, so --help, --version and every error message are byte-identical.
payload.chose: Split the CLI into a 545-byte dist/cli.js stub + 76KB dist/fast.js (hooks, statusline) + 986KB dist/full.js, with the stub calling module.enableCompileCache() before either import. fast.ts owns only the exact argv shapes the shims emit and returns false for anything else, falling through to the full CLI.
payload.over: Lazy dynamic imports inside the existing single bundle (esbuild inlines them back, so nothing is saved), or a second hand-written hook implementation (two sources of truth for hook behavior).

payload.note: Done via content-compare, NOT the O(1) target. Per-append projection cost on a 25-session initiative: 3.24ms to 0.35ms (9.3x). Still O(sessions) — one read+compare per session file — but ~0.014ms/session vs ~0.13ms/session before. Scaling measured: 3 sess 0.10ms, 8 sess 0.16ms, 11 sess 0.18ms, 25 sess 0.36ms. True O(1) would need to know which session file a given event can change; renderSession takes the whole state, so that inference is not safe to assume. Residual left deliberately.

payload.because: Measured on a 25-session initiative: rendering every session costs 0.03ms, writing every session costs 3.2ms — the render is 100x cheaper than the write, so caching renders optimizes the wrong half. Targeted regeneration would need to infer which session files an event can change, but renderSession takes the whole InitiativeState, so that inference is unsound. Content-compare is provably output-identical — the file holds the same bytes either way — so no reader can observe it, and it needs no knowledge of which event touched what.
payload.chose: Skip projection writes whose bytes already match disk (read + compare before writeFileAtomic), leaving the render unconditional.
payload.over: Regenerating only the session file the append touched (true O(1)), or caching rendered output in memory across appends.

payload.text: T5 must SPLIT — the two halves have opposite risk. T5a (drop get_state at session start) is provably safe: getState digest is literally renderStatus(state), and the SessionStart hook is renderStatus(state, {repoMemory, sessionId, git}) — same function, superset options. Verified: zero digest lines absent from the injected block. Only edge case is the shared STATUS_CHAR_LIMIT=10,000 cap; today's block is 3,923 bytes (39%), so past the cap the block clips its tail while a bare digest has more room. T5b (drop start_session) would REINTRODUCE the record-integrity bug: start_session's real job is ctx.session.set(), and resolveWriteInitiative falls back to branch bindings when there is no active session — bindings move (mine moved today via sofar new). Also appendAndProject would stamp session:'cli', detaching decisions/tasks from the session and breaking the Stop write-back linkage. The workaround (sessions.json index) is already a rejected approach. T4 marginal value fell after T1: hook is now 27.8ms not 64.5ms, so T4 saves ~21ms not ~57ms. node boot alone is 20ms of that 27.8ms, and curl's own spawn is 4.7 of T4's 6.9ms — so T4's entire value is escaping node boot and it cannot go below ~5ms.

payload.because: get_state digest is renderStatus(state) and the hook is renderStatus(state, {repoMemory, sessionId, git}) — same projection, superset options, verified empirically as zero digest lines absent from the injected block, so the call can only return less. But start_session's load-bearing effect is ctx.session.set(), not its event: without an active session resolveWriteInitiative falls back to the branch binding (which moves mid-session — it moved in this repo today) and appendAndProject stamps envelope.session "cli", detaching decisions and tasks from the session and breaking the Stop write-back linkage. That is the record-integrity misroute class, and its side-index workaround is already rejected. MCP-less AGENTS.md tools get no hook injection, so their orient-first step stays.
payload.chose: T5a only: the MCP protocol block now tells agents NOT to call sofar_get_state at session start (the SessionStart hook already injected renderStatus with strictly more options), while keeping sofar_start_session mandatory. AGENTS.md dialect untouched.
payload.over: T5b — also dropping sofar_start_session to save a second round trip.
